source: Wang & Uzzi (2026) Inventive Problem Solving with LLMs: A Benchmark for TRIZ Reasoning (TRIZBench), ACL Findings
finding: Largest TRIZ benchmark so far. Built from 1,354 expert-written TRIZ cases (590 source documents) and 429 US patents. Three tasks: predict the contradiction, predict inventive principles, and justify with cited patent sentences.
numbers: 1,354 cases; 1,679 contradictions; only 491 (29.2%) have TRIZ parameter IDs; 734 cases (54.2%) have principle labels; 429 patents (257 with parameters, 304 with principles). Expert audit of N=200 cases: raw inter-annotator agreement 74.0% before adjudication.
limits: Cases were extracted by Gemini-2.5-pro, then human-checked. Uses the classic 39x39 matrix only (newer matrix is copyrighted). 80/20 split. Gold labels come from the TRIZ literature, which is itself subjective.
agent_relevance: Gives a real test bed for an O4/O8 reframe step: we can score whether the model named the right trade-off and the right principle instead of judging by feel.

source: Wang & Uzzi (2026) Inventive Problem Solving with LLMs: A Benchmark for TRIZ Reasoning (TRIZBench), ACL Findings
finding: Detecting THAT a contradiction exists is easy. Recovering the correct improving/worsening PAIR is hard, especially on patent text.
numbers: Case-level contradiction detection F1 0.75-0.90 across Qwen3-8B/32B, LLaMA3.1-8B/70B, Gemini-2.5-Pro (zero-shot and few-shot). Pair F1 only 0.29-0.45. Patent-level pair Hit@3 only 0.13-0.28. Best: LoRA-tuned LLaMA3.1-8B detection F1 0.90, patent Hit@3 0.28; Gemini-2.5-Pro few-shot pair F1 0.42, Hit@3 0.24.
limits: Table layout in the PDF text is garbled, so the row-to-model mapping is my best reading. Text says few-shot gains are small and sometimes inconsistent. Pair match uses embedding similarity at a 0.65 threshold (95% of a sample judged valid by a human).
agent_relevance: Naming the trade-off is the weak link. A typed reframe should make the model state both sides of the trade-off explicitly and let code check that both are present, not trust one fluent sentence.

source: Wang & Uzzi (2026) Inventive Problem Solving with LLMs: A Benchmark for TRIZ Reasoning (TRIZBench), ACL Findings
finding: For choosing inventive principles, the old contradiction-matrix lookup beats direct LLM prompting. The best result is the LLM used as a reranker over matrix candidates.
numbers: Hit@3 on cases / patents: matrix lookup 0.67 / 0.48; Qwen3-8B zero-shot 0.39 / 0.27; Qwen3-8B few-shot 0.51 / 0.25; Gemini-2.5-Pro zero-shot 0.45 / 0.31; Gemini few-shot 0.52 / 0.35; Qwen3-8B Matrix-Rerank 0.71 / 0.59. End-to-end (predict pair, then matrix, then rerank): Qwen3-8B 0.59 / 0.46 zero-shot, 0.65 / 0.52 LoRA. Recall@3 for Matrix-Rerank 0.29 / 0.47.
quote: Direct LLM prompting underperforms across domains, ... plausible but weakly anchored principles
limits: Metric is whether any gold principle lands in the top 3 of 40, which is generous. Gold = principles the source author used, not necessarily the best ones. A Qwen3-8B reranker beat Gemini-2.5-Pro prompting, so model size is not the driver.
agent_relevance: Strong support for G5 and the program/model split: code does the lookup (a table), the model only selects among table candidates. Free-form 'think of a principle' is the weaker pattern.

source: Wang & Uzzi (2026) Inventive Problem Solving with LLMs: A Benchmark for TRIZ Reasoning (TRIZBench), ACL Findings
finding: Grounding check: asking models to cite patent sentences that support the chosen principle. Evidence quality rises with more cited sentences and with a better retriever. A right label does not mean right reasoning.
numbers: Positive link between evidence F1 and principle Hit@3 (shown in a figure, no exact slope given). PatentSBERTa grounded attribution was best; TF-IDF gave modest gains. Example: a case with correct parameter pair and Hit@3=1 still missed the evidence for the improving side; another had evidence F1=1.0 with a wrong parameter pair.
limits: Evidence sets are themselves built by retrieval from the case anchors, so the check is partly circular. A small qualitative calibration study (5 cases, 6 human participants) is in the appendix, not read.
agent_relevance: Supports G2/G3: a reframe should cite the exact source text it relies on, and code should check that the citation exists. Label accuracy alone can mislead.

source: Chen et al. (2024) TRIZ-GPT: An LLM-augmented method for problem-solving, ASME IDETC-CIE
finding: First systematic test of GPT-4 on the TRIZ workflow: problem to TRIZ parameters, contradiction pairs, inventive principles, then solutions. Built two case sets: 37 classic cases and 10 cases published after April 2023 (after the model's training cutoff).
numbers: Collection A 37 cases (3 used for few-shot, 34 tested); collection B 10 post-April-2023 cases; 47 cases in total.
limits: Ground truth is whatever the source paper authors wrote, not a single right answer. No human expert grading; computational metrics only.
agent_relevance: Shows a post-cutoff check on TRIZ cases, a model for keeping memorised textbook answers from inflating scores.

source: Chen et al. (2024) TRIZ-GPT
finding: Prompt strategy test for the contradiction-analysis step on GPT-4 (34 cases). Chain-of-thought and plain prompts found the literature's contradiction parameters; few-shot lowered recall because the model copied the example's number of pairs.
numbers: Recall / precision: basic 0.675 / 0.259; CoT 0.691 / 0.310; few-shot 0.245 / 0.333; CoT+few-shot 0.247 / 0.298. At least half the literature parameters found in 85.3% of cases (basic) and 88.2% (CoT).
quote: The lower recall scores observed with the few-shot strategy may stem from the LLMs unintentionally learning the number of contradiction pairs
limits: Recall is rewarded because ALL generated parameters were fed into the next step, so precision is low by design. Step 3 was run at a lower temperature than the solution step.
agent_relevance: A concrete negative: a worked example in the prompt narrowed the output and cut recall by about 45 points. Few-shot exemplars can anchor the count and shape of a reframe.

source: Chen et al. (2024) TRIZ-GPT
finding: Solution step: GPT-4, given the literature's principle, writes solutions that are semantically close to the original solution, and prompt strategy made no difference. Model size mattered for contradiction analysis (GPT-4 vs GPT-3.5).
numbers: Cosine similarity (text-embedding-ada-002) to the original solution across 84 case-principle items: base M=0.829 SD=0.031; CoT 0.823 SD=0.031; few-shot 0.824 SD=0.030; CoT+few-shot 0.824 SD=0.033. Collection B contradiction recall: GPT-4 0.544 vs GPT-3.5 0.400 (CoT).
limits: Embedding similarity of 0.82+ is typical for almost any two on-topic technical texts, so it is a weak test of whether the solution is right. Authors say expert grading was impractical across fields.
agent_relevance: Cheap similarity scores cannot tell a good reframe-derived solution from a plain one. Needs an outcome check (G3), not text similarity.

source: Chen et al. (2024) TRIZ-GPT - case study (in-pipe robot)
finding: Case study on an in-pipe robot: GPT-4 solutions matched the original paper's solution closely and added extra mechanisms; GPT-3.5 gave fewer contradiction pairs and sometimes did not follow the prompt format.
numbers: GPT-4 produced more contradiction pairs than GPT-3.5; GPT-3.5 identified only one of the paper's pairs; one case.
limits: One case, qualitative. The 2023 source paper could be in training data (the post-cutoff check was only done for collection B).
agent_relevance: Weaker models fail the format of a typed reframe; the schema should validate structure in code.

source: Jiang, Li, Qian, Zhang & Luo (2025) AutoTRIZ: Automating Engineering Innovation with TRIZ and LLMs (v4; Adv. Eng. Informatics)
finding: AutoTRIZ is a fixed four-module pipeline run by GPT-4: (1) find the contradiction, (2) pick the parameter pair, (3) look up principles from the matrix with code, (4) write solutions. Code, not the model, does the matrix lookup and report layout.
numbers: Four modules; matrix lookup deterministic; 40 principles, 39 parameters. Initial case base of 10 textbook cases across domains.
limits: Model used: GPT-4. A co-author who is a domain expert checked results. Earlier versions reported human-versus-LLM ideation comparisons; v4 lists novelty/usefulness comparison as future work.
agent_relevance: Closest published match to our idea of typed reframes with code-checked steps: the model fills slots, the program does the lookup. Good architecture reference for O4/O8.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) AutoTRIZ
finding: Contradiction detection is unstable across runs. The authors ran each problem 100 times and measured the entropy of the answers. 7 of 10 textbook cases had a match or half-match to the textbook within the top 3 detections. Higher-probability detections matched the textbook better.
numbers: 100 runs per case; entropy range 0 to 6.64 bits (higher = less consistent); 7/10 cases match or half-match in top 3; cases 5-8 had a clearly dominant top answer (two complete matches). In almost all cases one parameter stayed fixed while the other varied.
limits: Only 10 cases; textbook analysis is not a gold standard (authors say so). They chose NOT to majority-vote, because different valid contradictions give different valid solutions.
agent_relevance: One model, same prompt, gives many different 'contradictions' (G4). Frequency across samples can be a confidence signal, but diversity is also a feature in reframing. Count in code; do not ask the model which is best.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) AutoTRIZ
finding: Battery thermal-management case: AutoTRIZ proposals led the authors to a flat-heat-pipe design they then simulated. Reported gains over two published schemes. Human in the loop, one case, authors chose which idea to follow.
numbers: Proposed design vs best existing: about +24%, +64%, +26% on three metrics (grouping efficiency and volumetric energy density +20-30%, thermal management efficiency +60% or more). One case study, simplified model by the authors.
limits: Single case. No plain-GPT-4 run under the same conditions (they only report that guiding plain ChatGPT needed more detail from the engineer). Authors warn solutions may contain hallucinated or wrong content.
agent_relevance: Anecdotal in the same way the older TRIZ evidence is: success stories, no controlled comparison.

source: Szczepanik & Chudziak (2025) TRIZ Agents: A Multi-Agent LLM Approach for TRIZ-Based Innovation
finding: A team of GPT-4o agents (project manager, mechanical, control, safety engineers, TRIZ specialist, document specialist) walks six TRIZ steps on a gantry-crane problem. Compared by hand with the original case study.
numbers: Two runs. Step 4 found 2 contradictions (Speed vs Stability; Load capacity vs Safety), not an exact match but close. Step 6: one of the case study's three solutions found exactly (sliding mode control with antiswing), one missed (intelligent circuit breaker), one partly (thermal management). Six useful function links missed, one harmful link missed.
limits: One case, two runs, no scores, no single-agent baseline, no blind judge. Matrix lookup was a deterministic tool, so not compared. The TRIZ specialist rarely used its RAG tool when given the choice.
agent_relevance: Agents given freedom to skip a tool skipped it. For O4/O8, make the lookup compulsory in code. The missed solution belonged to the electrical specialist who was never called.

source: Trapp & Warschat (2024) LLM-based Extraction of Contradictions from Patents (Hagen)
finding: Zero-shot GPT-4 (gpt-4-1106-preview) in one prompt finds contradiction sentences in patents, summarises them and maps them to the 39 parameters. It matches or slightly beats the older fine-tuned PaTRIZ BERT models.
numbers: 100 patents from PaGAN (1,600 with contradictions). Annotated sentences average 3.81; GPT-4 found 2.69 (recall 0.71), plus 3.19 extra (precision 0.46), F1 0.56. PaTRIZ best part-models F1 0.37 and 0.65, weighted average 0.54. BERTScore F1 vs annotated sentences 0.93 (precision 0.93, recall 0.88); vs GPT summary 0.88.
limits: BERTScore 0.93 is a loose similarity measure and flatters the result; sentence-level F1 0.56 is the honest number. Only 100 of 1,600 patents, one model, no human check of parameter assignment.
agent_relevance: Same pattern as TRIZBench: spotting a trade-off in text is fairly easy for a model; precision is the issue (more than half the flagged sentences were not annotated).

source: Trapp & Warschat (2024) - prior computational systems for TRIZ contradictions
finding: Before LLMs, computer systems for TRIZ were rule-based or tuned BERT: SummaTRIZ and PaTRIZ find contradiction sentences in patents. They did well for problem and solution sentences but contradictions stayed hard.
numbers: PaTRIZ best part-models F1 0.37 ('first part', 2,276 positives) and 0.65 ('second part', 3,709 negatives); weighted average 0.54.
limits: Authors describe PaTRIZ as giving mixed results. Different dataset from TRIZBench, so numbers cannot be compared directly.
agent_relevance: Contradiction spotting was always the hard step, before and after LLMs.

source: Xu, Wu & Zhao (2026) TRIZ-RAGNER: retrieval-augmented LLM for TRIZ-aware NER in patent contradiction mining
finding: Retrieval of TRIZ knowledge plus reranking plus a structured prompt beats plain GPT and tuned sequence taggers at extracting improving/worsening parameters on PaTRIZ.
numbers: Pair-level F1: BiLSTM-CRF 60.7; BERT-CRF 68.5; RoBERTa-CRF 71.7; GPT zero-shot 73.7; GPT + prompt engineering 76.9; TRIZ-RAGNER 84.2 (P 85.6, R 82.9). Ablation F1: no retrieval 78.1; no rerank 79.8; no structured prompt 76.6. 3 seeds; about 3,000 sentences, 8:1:1 split.
limits: Preprint with warning signs: the results text describes a figure about 'cumulative systemic loss ratio', which looks pasted from another paper. Model name not given ('GPT'). Single dataset. Treat numbers as unverified.
agent_relevance: If the numbers hold, the structured prompt was worth about 7.6 F1 and retrieval about 6 F1 inside this one pipeline. Weak evidence.

source: Lee et al. (2026) Enhancing Creativity in 3D Generative Design via a TRIZ-Inspired Text-to-CAD Framework (KAIST)
finding: Strength-versus-weight contradiction on a chair. Four TRIZ principles, each given to an LLM that edits CAD code, compared with a vanilla 'make it lighter' prompt. The vanilla prompt just shrank dimensions; the TRIZ prompts made structural changes.
numbers: TRIZ variants: segmentation -14.7% mass, stress -0.1%; anti-weight -5.9% mass, +21.6% stress; dynamics -4.0%, +33.2%; composite materials -10.0%, +40.7%. Vanilla: -31.8% mass, +64.1% stress, +99.4% displacement. Baseline 16.93 kg, 0.627 MPa. FEA in ANSYS, 900 N load.
limits: One chair, one run per variant, no repeats, no human creativity rating. The vanilla prompt removed MORE mass; TRIZ won only on stress per kg removed and on being structurally different. All stresses stayed under 2% of yield, so safety was easy to keep.
agent_relevance: Honest control result: the reframe changed what kind of answer came out (structure, not scaling) but not how much was gained. A typed reframe widens the answer space; an outcome check must say whether it is better.

source: Liu, Huang & Wang (2026) TRIZa: Guiding Agent Evolution from Pattern Recognition to Solution Invention
finding: TRIZ matrix and 40 principles used as typed mutation operators inside an LLM evolutionary code-search loop (FunSearch/AlphaEvolve style), with hard promotion gates. Tested on three cybersecurity datasets.
numbers: Paired-rerun gains: PowerDuck GOOSE weighted-F1 0.9694 to 0.9982 (+2.88 pts); CICIoT2023 macro-F1 0.8326 to 0.8749 (+4.23); CIC-DDoS2019 0.7470 to 0.7485 (+0.15). 45-activity CICIoT campaign: macro-F1 0.8325 to 0.8483 (+0.0158, 1.90% relative); 43 of 45 family-seed groups improved; but it FAILED its frozen promotion gate (needed 3.2277% relative gain and a 0.005 FPR drop).
quote: does not determine whether the improvements came from TRIZ guidance, FI/Ideality, or another part of the workflow
limits: The authors state the comparisons do not show whether gains came from TRIZ guidance, the Functional Information/Ideality scoring, or the rest of the workflow. No control with random or untyped mutation. Single group, preprint.
agent_relevance: Closest published use of TRIZ inside an agent loop. Its own text admits the missing ablation (TRIZ vs untyped mutation), which is the test we would need for O4/O8.

source: Liu et al. (2026) TRIZa - loop design and controller results
finding: Loop design: the agent first names the technical contradiction (parameter to improve versus parameter that worsens), the matrix maps it to principles, the principle steers the code change, and a gate separates 'metric went up' from 'promote this change'. Useful and harmful function are scored on separate channels.
numbers: Controller Campaign08: original V1 gate promotion F1 0.508; a stricter variant had specificity 0.998 but recall 0.257 and promotion F1 0.409; balanced V2 reached promotion F1 0.811, recall 0.686, specificity 0.989. A later sequence V17 to V18 got worse on macro-F1, MCC and FPR.
limits: Controller tuning was done on the same campaigns it is scored on. Ideality (the ideal final result idea) is used as a score, not as a reframing step.
agent_relevance: Ideal final result as a measurable benefit-minus-harm score with a hard gate is a code-checkable form of the IFR idea, in line with G3/G5.

source: Bose (2026) IdeaForge: knowledge-graph multi-agent framework for cross-methodology innovation analysis
finding: TRIZ, Design Thinking and SCAMPER agents write claims into a graph; claims from different methods that are semantically close are linked as convergent. Used as an agreement signal across methods.
numbers: Five use cases, 16-node graphs, 3 claims each. Four of five reached full convergence (3 convergent pairs); the healthcare sepsis case only 1 pair; top InnovationScore 0.353-0.500. Run on TinyLlama via Ollama, threshold 0.65.
limits: TinyLlama (a tiny model); no human or expert rating; no baseline numbers, only a qualitative comparison to single-method runs; InnovationScore is a heuristic with hand-set weights. Convergence in 4 of 5 may just mean one small model gives similar outputs.
agent_relevance: Warning for G4: methods agreeing is weak evidence when all voices come from one model. Do not count TRIZ-vs-SCAMPER agreement as independent confirmation.

source: Mohammadi & Zeng (2025) Enhancing TRIZ through environment-based design methodology supported by a large language model, AI EDAM 39:e12
finding: GPT-3.5 pipeline: ask EBD-style questions, extract interactions, build a functional analysis, the designer picks a contradiction, then run each of the 40 principles separately. Rated by experts on three design problems taken from 11 TRIZ-solved textbook problems.
numbers: Functional analysis accuracy about 50% (rated by a TRIZ expert); item counts per case: 310/108 unique, 252/128, 140/81. Ideas: LLM variety and quantity exceeded the TRIZ expert's and were more novel (Shah metrics); quality ranged from very high to low, with ideas that did not resolve the contradiction scored zero. Runtime 40-50 minutes for all 40 principles.
limits: Three problems, two raters, GPT-3.5 only, compared with short static textbook solutions (biased toward the LLM on counts). Exact table values for question and idea scores were not in the text I read. Authors call 50% functional-analysis accuracy inadequate.
agent_relevance: Running all 40 principles blindly gives many ideas but many bad ones. Filter by contradiction type first, and score by code.

source: Wang & Uzzi (2026) Inventive Problem Solving with LLMs: A Benchmark for TRIZ Reasoning (TRIZBench), ACL Findings - related-work survey
finding: The authors say earlier TRIZ-LLM papers (AutoTRIZ, TRIZ-GPT, Lee et al. 2024 eco-design, Guo et al. 2025 road cone) largely rely on small case collections and domain-specific scenarios, with qualitative analysis.
numbers: Case counts in the earlier work in this file: 10 (AutoTRIZ), 47 (TRIZ-GPT), 3 (EBD-LLM), 1 (TRIZ Agents), 1 (Text-to-CAD), 5 use cases (IdeaForge).
limits: Summary by authors of a competing benchmark.
agent_relevance: No randomised or blinded study with human designers testing LLM+TRIZ against LLM without TRIZ was found. Every result in this file is a case or a benchmark.

source: Gap note: no LLM study of the TRIZ ideal-final-result step alone
finding: An arXiv web search for the exact phrase 'ideal final result' returned only three 2013-2014 TRIZ-in-software papers and nothing on LLMs. IFR appears in LLM work only as a score (TRIZa Ideality) or as a prompt step inside larger pipelines.
numbers: arXiv title/abstract search: 3 hits, all 2013-2014 (virus-scanning, keyboard and menu patent analyses).
limits: Search tools were rate-limited (Semantic Scholar 429, OpenAlex budget gone, arXiv API empty), so coverage is by arXiv web search plus Crossref. Non-arXiv papers may exist.
agent_relevance: The ideal-final-result prompt ('imagine the problem solves itself') has no measured LLM effect that we found. We would have to test it ourselves.
